## Repository findings

This checkout contains **no application source or existing game**: there is no `package.json`, app entry point, HTML page, framework config, or game code. The only tracked project files are the README and OpenCode workflow; the other root-level files are local runner scaffolding.

### Key files

- [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md) — identifies the project as an OMGithub-created project, but provides no technical or app details.

- [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/Agents.md`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/Agents.md) — runner guidance. It mentions a Pascal development server at `http://localhost:3002` and browser capture expectations, but that server or app is not present in this checkout. It also calls out mobile support, responsive layouts, touch controls, and safe areas.
- [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh) — invokes an externally provided `${RUNTIME_DIR}/scripts/default-start.mjs`; it is not a project-specific start command.
- [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh) — similarly delegates capture to `${RUNTIME_DIR}/scripts/default-capture.mjs`.
- [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/startup.sh`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/startup.sh) — only enables strict shell mode; no startup logic.
- [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/package.json`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/package.json) — a **separate skill-tool package** that includes Three.js 0.184 and GLTF tooling. It is not the game’s dependency manifest.
- [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/SKILL.md`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/SKILL.md) — documents Three.js/PlayCanvas model integration and browser verification; potentially useful if the game uses GLB assets, but it does not supply game code.

## Run and test commands

There are no repository-defined install, build, test, or app-run commands. `./start.sh` and `./capture.sh` require the runner’s `RUNTIME_DIR` and its external scripts, so they are not standalone project commands. The agent guidance recommends browser capture with `playwright-cli` at port 3002, but the corresponding app/server is absent.

## Recommendations for the game

Start by creating the app scaffold and choosing a renderer. **Three.js with a lightweight TypeScript/Vite setup** is a reasonable fit: it aligns with the repository’s GLB guidance and is suitable for a mobile browser game. Treat the existing skill package as tooling, not as the game’s dependency setup.

For a polished but achievable open-world prototype:

- Build a stylized, procedural city from reusable low-poly building blocks; prioritize readable streets, rooftops, skyline, lighting, and atmosphere over a huge detailed map.
- Implement a clear movement loop: running/jumping, anchor selection, tether attach/release, gravity and momentum, and forgiving controls. Add collision handling and a camera that anticipates swing direction.
- Make the game usable on phones from the outset: responsive HUD, visible touch controls, safe-area spacing, and alternatives to motion/tilt input.
- Keep performance bounded with simple materials, instancing or batching for repeated city geometry, limited shadows, and device-aware rendering resolution.
- Add a small objective loop—such as collectibles or timed rooftop challenges—so the world has a playable goal, not just free movement.
- Establish browser-based acceptance checks for loading, visible geometry, movement, swinging, touch input, and a narrow-screen layout before expanding content.
